neighbours.label: sentence-initial ' This' right after a sentence describing a physical or physiological mechanism, where a consequence is about to be stated ('… This causes'); the - pole takes ' This' after a reported finding ('… This may be because')
fire: When the artery narrows, less blood reaches the heart muscle. This starves the tissue of oxygen.
Cold water sinks beneath the warmer layer near the surface. This drives a slow current along the sea floor.
The disc bulges outward and presses on the spinal cord. This produces weakness in the legs.
As the ice melts, the dark ocean absorbs more sunlight. This speeds up the warming.
The enzyme can no longer break down the sugar in milk. This leads to bloating and cramps.
Moist air is forced upward when it meets the mountains. This cools it until rain falls.
The lens of the eye stiffens with age and cannot change shape. This makes close objects look blurred.
Roots take up water faster than the dry soil can supply it. This lowers the pressure inside the stem.
quiet: Patients in the treatment group reported less pain after a month. This suggests the drug is effective.
The second survey found fewer birds than the first. This may reflect the cold spring.
We drove to the coast on Saturday. This time the weather was kind to us.
Older children did no better than younger ones on the task. This was a surprise to the authors.
My sister called me late last night. This morning she called again.
The mice given the supplement lived no longer than the others. This result contradicts earlier work.
The committee met for three hours on Tuesday. This week it will meet again.
Students who took notes by hand remembered more. This finding has been repeated several times.

notes: Probes: ' This' after mechanism sentences 0.38-0.54 (also with nothing after it); after a study result 0.01; 'This morning' after narrative 0.01. 'this nerve' 0.26, so some content nouns in mechanism text fire too.
